datumFramework.role: Primary fixed structural and machining reference plane for the kinetic mechanism.
datumFramework.rule: Datum A must resolve to qualified fixed structure and must not reference decorative canopy skin, false ceiling, removable trim or service panels.

datumFramework.role: Functional vertical rotation axis shared by the bearing, carrier, direct-carrier brake and feedback coordination model.
datumFramework.rule: Datum B currently controls axis direction only. Its physical XY location/feature remains TBD until bearing and structural support geometry are selected and controlled; the composition origin must not be substituted and no fabricated bore or bolt circle may be inferred from it.

datumFramework.role: Angular service and reference-index datum tied to the controlled product orientation.
datumFramework.rule: Datum C must be physically recoverable after power restoration and must not imply that arriving at the index means the mechanical service lock is engaged.

datumFramework.role: Functional rotating carrier interface plane used to coordinate axial stack and service envelopes.
datumFramework.rule: The existing 24 mm carrier thickness parameter is not Datum D and must not be used as the available mechanism stack height.

mechanicalInterfaces.function: Primary gravity, radial and overturning-load transfer while permitting continuous vertical-axis rotation.
mechanicalInterfaces.reactionPath: rotating carrier -> bearing -> fixed structural support -> site structure
prohibitedCommonCause: motor/reducer as vertical support
decorative canopy skin as bearing support
secondary-retention attachment relying only on the same local failed bearing bolts
mechanicalInterfaces.serviceRequirement: Bearing fasteners, lubrication points where applicable, mounting face/runout references and removal path must remain inspectable and serviceable.

mechanicalInterfaces.function: Apply commanded propulsion torque through a positive transmission without becoming the primary support or access restraint.
rotatingSide: dedicated synchronous toothed ring or ring gear under qualification
mechanicalInterfaces.reactionPath: drive tangential force and pretension reactions -> fixed drive bracket and carrier drive ring -> qualified structural supports
prohibitedCommonCause: gearbox self-locking used as service lock
drive transmission used as sole fault holding path
unaccounted belt pretension transferred into bearing/support design
mechanicalInterfaces.serviceRequirement: Tension/alignment adjustment, guard removal, drive-module extraction and inspection must be possible without disturbing controlled cable exits.

mechanicalInterfaces.function: Provide power-off holding and qualified fault-stop action directly at the carrier independently of a failed drive transmission where required by risk assessment.
fixedSide: spring-applied electrically released caliper or equivalent
mechanicalInterfaces.reactionPath: carrier brake ring -> fixed brake caliper/bracket -> fixed structural support
prohibitedCommonCause: fault holding torque forced only through belt/gear transmission
brake treated as the mechanical service lock
rotating electrical release power
mechanicalInterfaces.serviceRequirement: Friction surfaces, wear/air-gap state, brake-state sensing where selected and guarded manual release must be inspectable without uncontrolled carrier motion.

mechanicalInterfaces.function: Provide positive mechanical restraint for technician access after zero speed verification and isolation.
fixedSide: fixed double-shear or equivalently justified bracket
rotatingSide: dedicated receiver ring/lugs structurally isolated from precision feedback and brake friction surfaces
mechanicalInterfaces.reactionPath: carrier service load -> receiver -> positive lock -> fixed structural bracket -> site structure
prohibitedCommonCause: motor torque used as access restraint
brake status substituted for lock engagement
lock reaction through precision bearing rolling elements where avoidable
software index flag treated as physical engagement
mechanicalInterfaces.serviceRequirement: Engagement must be captive, visually obvious, LOTO-compatible and directly verifiable before access; partial engagement must be geometrically detectable or prevented.

mechanicalInterfaces.function: Arrest abnormal carrier separation or tilt after relevant primary-support failure without routine running contact.
rotatingSide: multiple distributed passive capture features on qualified carrier structure
mechanicalInterfaces.reactionPath: abnormally displaced carrier -> distributed capture features -> fixed catch sectors -> fixed structural support
prohibitedCommonCause: all capture attachments lost with one relevant bearing-ring failure
all capture attachments sharing only the same failed bearing bolts
decorative skin used as catch structure
routine retention rubbing used as normal support
mechanicalInterfaces.serviceRequirement: Normal clearance and contact witness must be inspectable; any engagement removes the fixture from service pending engineering inspection.

mechanicalInterfaces.function: Measure carrier position, speed and reference/index state using fixed powered electronics and passive rotating features.
mechanicalInterfaces.reactionPath: measurement only; no structural, brake or restraint reaction path permitted
prohibitedCommonCause: sensor bracket used as carrier restraint
powered rotating encoder introduced without architecture change
index signal used as proof of service-lock engagement
mechanicalInterfaces.serviceRequirement: Readhead air gap, alignment, contamination state and replacement adjustment must be inspectable from fixed-side service access.

mechanicalInterfaces.function: Provide independent or sufficiently diverse speed/overspeed plausibility if allocated by the released risk assessment.
fixedSide: independent/diverse fixed sensor channel if required
rotatingSide: passive target set sufficiently independent from the primary feedback failure mode if required
mechanicalInterfaces.reactionPath: measurement only; no mechanical load path
prohibitedCommonCause: blindly duplicating the same single failure mechanism
sharing one software value while claiming independent measurement
powered rotating target electronics
mechanicalInterfaces.serviceRequirement: Channel identity and diagnostic disagreement must be testable without dismantling the carrier.

mechanicalInterfaces.function: Permit controlled balance correction while preserving all 240 controlled cable-exit coordinates.
mechanicalInterfaces.reactionPath: trim mass inertial/gravity loads -> dedicated carrier trim station -> carrier structure
prohibitedCommonCause: moving cable exits to correct balance
loose/unretained trim weights
trim hardware obstructing service lock or retention
mechanicalInterfaces.serviceRequirement: Trim mass, station ID and fastener state must be recordable and replaceable under the service-lock/LOTO state.

mechanicalInterfaces.function: Maintain inspection, tooling and component-extraction paths for all kinetic modules without treating removable architecture as structure.
mechanicalInterfaces.reactionPath: no primary structural reaction through removable service panels or false ceiling
prohibitedCommonCause: service panel used as primary structure
electrical tray used as mechanical reaction support
removal path requiring uncontrolled carrier movement
mechanicalInterfaces.serviceRequirement: Normal replaceable kinetic modules must have a demonstrated extraction and reinstallation path with carrier positively locked and isolated.

interfaceParameters.unit: mm XY relative to a future controlled fixed-structure datum
interfaceParameters.dependency: selected bearing/support architecture plus controlled mechanical datum drawing; composition origin is not sufficient evidence
selected bearing mounting requirement plus support stiffness calculation
exact bearing variant and supplier fastening procedure
approved torque, transmission ratio, selected tooth geometry and package study
approved torque and exact transmission selection
exact synchronous transmission selection and supplier calculation
approved holding/fault-stop torque and selected brake family
exact selected brake friction interface, thermal duty and ring structural check
selected brake mating geometry and final axial stack
approved service load case, material and proof methodology
bearing/carrier runout, structural deflection and complete tolerance stack
failure-state geometry and approved abnormal load case
selected primary sensor family and runout/concentricity stack
risk allocation and selected diverse sensing technology
production mass variation and balance correction calculation
selected component dimensions, tooling and fixed canopy frame layout

toleranceClosures.acceptanceSource: exact bearing supplier mounting requirements plus approved structural/machining calculation and measured prototype inspection
selected transmission supplier alignment/runout requirements plus prototype measurement
selected brake supplier disc/ring runout and air-gap requirements plus measured assembly runout
approved lock geometry, tolerance calculation and physical full/partial engagement validation
approved normal-operation no-contact requirement plus failure-engagement geometry and measured prototype clearances
selected sensor supplier air-gap/runout specification plus measured full-rotation verification
controlled service-access study using exact selected component CAD and representative tooling

failureStateModels.purpose: Verify normal rotating clearances and that secondary retention remains non-contact.
mustRemainTrue: no removable service panel is a load path

failureStateModels.purpose: Verify loss/separation of the drive transmission does not remove the required direct-carrier holding path.
mustRemainTrue: required holding path bypasses the failed transmission
service lock remains a separate access control

failureStateModels.purpose: Verify brake application clearances, reaction path and service access independently from propulsion.
mustRemainTrue: brake is not labelled mechanically locked for access
no rotating electrical power is required

failureStateModels.purpose: Verify positive lock engagement and technician-access geometry.
mustRemainTrue: positive mechanical restraint is directly verifiable
zero speed and isolation precede access
index position alone is not lock confirmation

failureStateModels.purpose: Model relevant abnormal primary-support displacement before and into secondary-retention engagement.
mustRemainTrue: retention attachments relevant to the model survive the represented primary failure
uncontained failure modes remain explicitly disclosed

failureStateModels.purpose: Verify post-engagement geometry, reaction path and inspection access.
mustRemainTrue: fixture is out of service after engagement
retention is not reused as normal running support without engineering disposition

failureStateModels.purpose: Verify recovery access without creating an uncontrolled freewheel state.
geometryToModel: controlled brake/drive release tooling if required
mustRemainTrue: carrier is positively restrained before manual release
normal holding path is restored before service lock removal

failureStateModels.purpose: Verify that sensing faults do not create physical interference and that diverse targets remain serviceable if allocated.
mustRemainTrue: no sensor is a mechanical restraint
fault reset cannot command or resume motion

serviceabilityRules: A stopped or electrically held carrier is not a safe-access state; positive service lock engagement and LOTO are required before mechanical access.
All normal replaceable kinetic modules should be removable from fixed-side service access without moving controlled cable exits or fixed LED coordinates.
Bearing fasteners, drive tension/alignment, brake wear state, retention clearance/contact witness, service-lock engagement and sensor air gaps require inspection access.
Manual recovery must never rely on uncontrolled freewheel; positive restraint precedes any manual brake or drive release.
Secondary-retention engagement is an out-of-service engineering-inspection condition and cannot be cleared by ordinary operator reset.
Safety-relevant mechanical state must have direct physical verification where required and must not rely on colour-only indication or a software label alone.
